value.why: To-date production and projection.
Voter pool and ballot timing determine what information can influence the award result.
A stable or rising role sustains per-game production for the rest of the season.
PP role is a stable driver of points that survives regression better than finishing.
Underlying chance quality for regression.
Finishing above skill regresses, so hot leaders should be discounted for rest-of-season projections.
Goalie awards and saves/wins leaderboards depend on goaltender quality and team defence.
Age and development priors anchor rest-of-season rate and the award narrative.
Games remaining depend on health; late injuries can end an award or leader race.
Team success correlates with award voting and with player opportunity.
Finalist and ballot dates decide when new information stops affecting the result.
Narrative-driving events can change voter preferences between close candidates.
Season totals are sums of over-dispersed per-game counts.
The core of the Jack Adams voter model and absent from the draft's player-production inputs.
Provides the first stage of the top-pick contract: which team will be on the clock.
Determines which franchise's selection a top-pick contract depends on, with conditionality evaluated on simulated standings.
Gives the second stage of the draft contracts: what the team on the clock does.
Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.
Gives the Vezina contract a goalie-specific production chain (rate, starts share, shrinkage) that skater inputs do not provide.
Supplies the rookie-specific prior and role inputs for the Calder contract that veteran production inputs lack.
Needed for the six award and stat title contracts because they resolve by voters, not by team quality.
KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS pays on the round's goal leader with 1/N ties; this simulation is the only input producing that functional.

Stage s4 and the final-delta formula of nhl.coach_expectation_delta: supplies the joint simulation of every team's remaining regular season (final points, correlated across coaches) from which each coach's simulated final delta is computed; it is the canonical simulator and replaces the DUPLICATE-flagged nhl.team_season_points_distribution, which this archetype no longer carries.

The roster-change term inside the in-house preseason expectation P_exp of nhl.coach_expectation_delta (minutes-weighted impact of arrivals minus departures, age curve) comes from this blend of last seasons' ratings with current-season data; used in stage s2 only to fix the expectation a coach is judged against before opening night.
